title: Smallness
text:
Our weeping is such a small thing;

sighs are such a small thing...

And yet, for such small things,

you and we die.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Spanish version's stark contrast between tiny gestures and mortal consequence.

title: Foreboding
text:
it is that long shadow

that little by little advances over

        the grass

when the sun abandons its empires...


it is the faint whisper

that runs through the fearful grass

        to tell it that night is coming.
editorial_note: The source credits Carlos López Narváez's Spanish version; the translation keeps the shadow and grass-whisper structure.

title: Certainty
text:
I have never seen a wasteland,

and the sea I never came to see,

but I have seen the eyes of the heather,

and I know what the waves must be.


I have never spoken with God,

nor visited Him in Heaven,

but I am sure where I am traveling,

as if the route had been given to me.
editorial_note: The translation follows the Spanish version's confidence in unseen landscape and destination.

title: It Is Good to Dream. To Wake Is Better...
text:
It is good to dream. To wake is better

if one wakes in the morning.

If we wake at midnight,

it is better to dream of dawn.


Sweeter the imagined robin

that never gladdened the tree

than to face the solidity of a dawn

that leads to no day at all.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the waking/dreaming paradox and the imagined robin against a dayless dawn.

title: In My Flower I Have Hidden...
text:
In my flower I have hidden

so that, if you carried me on your breast,

without suspecting it, I too would be there...

And only the angels will know the rest.


In my flower I have hidden

so that, when I slip from your vase,

you, without knowing it, may feel

almost the loneliness I have left you.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the flower as secret presence and later absence.
